summary: Scaniverse is Niantic Spatial's phone scanner, free on iOS and Android and now paired with a cloud service and a web application. It is the most complete free path from a phone in a pocket to a splat that other tools can read, and in 2026 it is two products under one name: 'Scaniverse Classic', which scans, trains and exports entirely on the device with no account needed for the scanning itself, and the new Scaniverse, where scans upload to Niantic Spatial's servers, several people's scans of one site are combined, and the result comes back as a Gaussian splat, a mesh, or a positioning map for the company's visual positioning service. It matters to this map for three reasons. It writes SPZ, the openly licensed splat container the rest of the industry has adopted, whose fourth version arrived in May 2026 with a plaintext header, parallel compression streams and a vendor extension chain — the only splat format scored here with an extension mechanism at all. It exports a USDZ package that carries a splat and an automatically aligned mesh together, aimed at robot simulation, which is the clearest example anywhere in this map of captured content reaching a conventional scene container without being thrown away. And it georeferences: a capture can be dragged onto a map until it sits where it really is, then serve as a positioning map. What it does not do is time — nothing here captures or carries a moving scene — and nothing it writes states a licence or an author.

coverage.note: The application draws splats and meshes on a phone and in a web browser, well enough to inspect a capture for holes and distortion. Nothing about that pipeline is described or exposed; it is a viewer inside a product.

coverage.note: Searched the Niantic Spatial documentation index (llms.txt), the 66 pages of the NSDK guide index (llms-nsdk.txt) and the 7 pages of the Scaniverse guide index (llms-scaniverse.txt) for POST and PUT requests, upload or create-site interfaces, programmatic, MCP and command-line terms on 2026-10-20; found scoped developer tokens and read-only Sites and mesh-download interfaces, with Site creation described only as a Scaniverse app and web task. Scaniverse capture and publishing of Sites is documented as a manual workflow, so an outside agent has no documented way to create or publish content.

coverage.note: Scaniverse is a capture app and service that exports files in formats defined as separate specifications, and it declares no extension scheme of its own. SPZ 4's extension records are the format's; Niantic says SPZ 4 export is still to be added to Scaniverse.

coverage.note: Scaniverse captures and returns scans as assets in sites; resolving scene resource identifiers belongs to a scene or container format that references those assets, which Scaniverse does not author.

sources.title: Niantic Spatial Scaniverse FAQ
sources.quote: Scaniverse Classic is designed for individual use, and best for reconstruction of objects and small environments and personal projects where you want to capture and view results quickly.

coverage.note: Sites are private by default, which is access control on the service and not a protection scheme declared inside content for recipients. Scaniverse exports open mesh and splat files.

sources.title: Scaniverse quickstart
sources.quote: Sites are private by default, meaning they’re accessible only to you and team members in your Organization.

sources.title: Scaniverse documentation: advanced tools
sources.quote: Supported exports include .ply , .spz , .glb , .fbx , and .usdz .

coverage.note: Scaniverse produces meshes, Gaussian splats and positioning maps, and its documented exports are PLY, SPZ, GLB, FBX and USDZ, none of which is a cell-volume representation. Searched the Scaniverse documentation (home, quickstart, advanced tools, techniques, 360 camera, troubleshooting, migration guide), the Scaniverse FAQ, the Lightship migration FAQ, the Capture product page and the USDZ blog post for voxel, volume, TSDF and occupancy on 2026-10-20; found no match.
